# job-tracker-student-mcp

> Job application tracker MCP server. Track internships, jobs, interviews and deadlines offline, with status updates and a list of what is coming up. No account. Free and open source, works with Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code and Windsurf.

## Setup
- Run with npx -y job-tracker-student-mcp
- Works offline, no account. No API keys, no passwords and no network calls.
- Applications are saved in one JSON file at ~/.job-tracker-student-mcp/applications.json. Set the JOB_TRACKER_FILE environment variable to use another path.
- add_application and update_status write to that file. list_upcoming and export_report only read it.

## Stages and dates
- An application is in one of four stages: applied, interview, offer or rejected.
- Dates are written as YYYY-MM-DD. An interview date can also have a time, written as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM.
- list_upcoming shows the deadline of applications in the applied stage and the interview date of applications in the interview stage. Offers and rejected applications are left out.

## Tools

### add_application
Add a job or internship to the tracker. It starts in the applied stage unless you pass another status. Inputs: company and role (both required), an optional deadline as YYYY-MM-DD, an optional source such as LinkedIn or a career fair, an optional type of job or internship, an optional status and optional notes. The tool saves the application on this computer and returns its id, which update_status needs. Example prompt: "Add a Software Intern role at Shopify with a deadline of 2026-11-15, found on LinkedIn."
Parameters: company, role, deadline, source, type, status, notes.
- company: Name of the company. Required.
- role: Title of the role. Required.
- deadline: Last day to apply as YYYY-MM-DD.
- source: Where you found the posting, such as LinkedIn or a career fair.
- type: "job" or "internship". Defaults to "job".
- status: The stage: "applied", "interview", "offer" or "rejected". Defaults to "applied".
- notes: Anything you want to remember about it.
Example call: `{"name":"add_application","arguments":{"company":"Shopify","role":"Software Intern","deadline":"2026-11-15","source":"LinkedIn","type":"internship"}}`
Output: One sentence naming the new application, its id, type, status and deadline.
Structured output: application with id, company, role, type, status, deadline, interview_date, source, notes, added and updated.

### update_status
Move an application to another stage: applied, interview, offer or rejected. Inputs: id of the application (from add_application or export_report), the new status, an optional interview_date as YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM, and an optional note that is added to the notes. When the status is interview, pass interview_date so list_upcoming can remind you. Example prompt: "Move application 1 to interview on 2026-11-20 at 14:30."
Parameters: id, status, interview_date, note.
- id: The id of the application. Required.
- status: The stage: "applied", "interview", "offer" or "rejected". Required.
- interview_date: Interview date as YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM.
- note: A note to add to the application.
Example call: `{"name":"update_status","arguments":{"id":1,"status":"interview","interview_date":"2026-11-20T14:30"}}`
Output: One sentence saying the application moved from one stage to another, with the interview date when there is one.
Structured output: previous_status, and application with id, company, role, type, status, deadline, interview_date, source, notes, added and updated.

### list_upcoming
Show upcoming deadlines and interviews sorted by date, with a reminder for each one. Deadlines come from applications still in the applied stage, and interviews come from applications in the interview stage that have an interview_date. Rejected applications and offers are left out. Inputs: optional days, how far ahead to look (default 14), include_overdue (default true) to also show deadlines that already passed, and an optional today as YYYY-MM-DD to ask as if it were another day. Example prompt: "What deadlines and interviews do I have in the next two weeks?"
Parameters: days, include_overdue, today.
- days: How many days ahead to look. Defaults to 14.
- include_overdue: Also show deadlines and interviews that already passed. Defaults to true.
- today: Treat this YYYY-MM-DD date as today. Defaults to today on this computer.
Example call: `{"name":"list_upcoming","arguments":{"days":14,"today":"2026-11-10"}}`
Output: A bullet list with one line per item, earliest first, each with a reminder such as due tomorrow or overdue by 2 days.
Structured output: today, and items with id, company, role, kind, when, days_left and reminder.

### export_report
Export your applications as CSV or Markdown so you can share them or open them in a spreadsheet. Inputs: format, either csv or markdown (default markdown), and an optional status to export only that stage. The report is returned as text and nothing is written to disk. In CSV, a cell that starts with =, +, - or @ gets a leading apostrophe so spreadsheets do not run it as a formula. Example prompt: "Export all my applications as a CSV."
Parameters: format, status.
- format: "csv" or "markdown". Defaults to "markdown".
- status: Only export applications in this stage.
Example call: `{"name":"export_report","arguments":{"format":"csv"}}`
Output: A sentence with the number of applications exported, then the report.
Structured output: format, count and content.

## FAQ

### Does it send reminders on its own?
No. An MCP server only answers when it is asked. list_upcoming gives the reminders when you ask for them.

### Is anything sent over the network?
No. The server reads and writes one local JSON file and makes no network calls.
